recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-18823 unless PA reopens the Appointment/Encounter status model in a later tracker; adding an Appointment in-progress code now would contradict this published decision.
issue_request: FHIR-18823 asked to add an Appointment in-progress status because arrived and fulfilled did not explicitly represent an appointment while care was underway. The final Published / Not Persuasive with Modification decision instead clarified that when Appointment.status is fulfilled, status tracking moves to the Encounter.
initial_application: The change appears to have been applied by cb628754c6856b96d7456ae810b6b80b8a4056d1, merged as 4bb5ace5bfe3b431ec777313612408dc119f7f90, which changed the fulfilled definition in the then-authoritative Appointment spreadsheet from the old completed/encounter wording to the approved encounter-tracks-status wording. Later source refactors preserved that definition in source/appointment/codesystem-appointmentstatus.xml.
additional_context: PA 2018 Baltimore WGM minutes discuss tracker 18823 directly, explain the rationale that once an appointment is fulfilled the Encounter tracks care status, note edge cases, and record the decision to make fulfilled clearer rather than add a separate Appointment in-progress status. Appointment is active in source/fhir.ini, and Appointment.status is required-bound to AppointmentStatus.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current active AppointmentStatus code system already contains the approved fulfilled definition, and the Appointment.status status list does not add an in-progress code, matching the published disposition.
